key_insight: QiT shows that quantum-inspired angle encoding, cosine-style attention, and multiplicative gating can be implemented as a scalable classical Transformer for vision, without running a quantum circuit.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical baseline for testing quantum-motivated inductive biases in image recognition while keeping standard Transformer complexity and hardware requirements.
method: Angle-inspired token encoding uses trigonometric features analogous to rotation-based quantum state preparation.
Self-attention operates on periodic features to approximate a cosine/fidelity kernel.
Gated multiplicative blocks emulate interaction terms seen in variational quantum circuits.
evidence_signal: On image-classification benchmarks, QiT is competitive with a matched classical Transformer and QiT-B reports 78.3% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with 45.7M parameters and 11.5 GFLOPs.
watch_item: The approach is not quantum and does not claim quantum speedup, so any gains should be interpreted as classical inductive-bias effects rather than evidence of quantum advantage.
paper_title: QiT: Quantum-Inspired Transformer for Visual Recognition Task
